newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UNION BOSS SAYS NO WAGE BATTLES PLANNED.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UNION BOSS SAYS NO WAGE BATTLES PLANNED.

text.p: A key Czech union boss said on Monday that while he did not agree with the centre-right government's austerity programme, he would not seek to intiate wider conflicts over the issue.
"We are not going to initiate wage battles," Richard Falbr, head of the Czech and Moravian Confederation of Trade Unions (CMKOS) told journalists after meeting government ministers.
"Still we don't agree with the government's steps," he added.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his government are trying to get labour to go along with an austerity programme of sharp budget cuts, wage freezes, and reductions in social security payments to stabilise the teetering economy and Czech crown.
The government announced its plans on May 28 aiming to slow domestic demand which has ballooned the current account deficit and made the crown ripe for speculators' attacks.
Union leaders and opposition politicians have railed against plans to deregulate rents and energy costs.

After the "Tripartite" meeting which included ministers, industry and labour representatives, Klaus repeated that his government would not veer from its plans, which include a total of 45.6 billion crowns in spending cuts from the original 1997 budget.
"The budget change is the maximum step which we can do now," Klaus told reporters after the meeting.
He again called on entreprenuers to temper wage increases in line with productivity, one of the country's largest macroeconomic problems.
"(Restrictive wage) measures in the state sector must be augemented by temperance in the private sector," Klaus said.
